llm.reply:
The retrieved trials are thyroid-cancer studies rather than trials explicitly targeting "carcinoma, not otherwise specified" as an entity, spanning radioimmunotherapy plus stem cell transplantation [1], thalidomide [2], irinotecan [3], tanespimycin [4], and suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid [5]. Alongside these, several disease records use the "Not Otherwise Specified" designation across different tumor types, including medullary carcinoma [6], primary intraosseous carcinoma derived from odontogenic cyst [7], primary intraosseous carcinoma derived from odontogenic keratocyst [9], advanced renal cell carcinoma [10], metastatic renal cell carcinoma [11], locally advanced renal cell carcinoma [12], and cervical squamous cell carcinoma [13], plus a separate breast carcinoma subtype [8].

## Trials retrieved

The five clinical trials returned all concern thyroid cancer treatment approaches rather than a generic "carcinoma NOS" indication, testing radioimmunotherapy with or without chemotherapy and stem cell transplantation [1], thalidomide [2], irinotecan in metastatic or inoperable disease [3], tanespimycin in advanced or metastatic disease [4], and suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid in advanced, recurrent, or metastatic disease [5].

## NOS disease entities

Multiple disease records carry the "Not Otherwise Specified" qualifier attached to distinct tumor sites, including medullary carcinoma NOS [6], which is also indexed as a MedGen concept [15], along with renal cell carcinoma variants at advanced, metastatic, and locally advanced stages [10][11][12], cervical squamous cell carcinoma NOS [13], and intraosseous carcinomas arising from odontogenic cysts or keratocysts [7][9].

## Prognostic context

A population-based study found that NOS breast carcinoma had a 5-year relative survival of 66%, markedly lower than special-type carcinomas, and that tumor morphology along with hormone receptor status remained significant predictors of survival even after adjusting for age and stage [17: "Morphology and hormone receptor status were confirmed as significant survival predictors in this population-based study, even after adjusting for age and stage at diagnosis"]. This finding derives from publication PMID 15365566 [16], whose title addresses prognostic value of morphology and hormone receptor status in breast cancer [14].

The retrieved trials are not specific to a disease coded as "carcinoma, not otherwise specified" but rather target thyroid cancer, using several distinct interventions.

## Retrieved trials

Radioimmunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy Plus Peripheral Stem Cell Transplantation in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer is one such trial [1]. Thalidomide in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer is another [2]. Irinotecan in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Inoperable Thyroid Cancer is listed as well [3]. Tanespimycin in Treating Patients With Inoperable Locoregionally Advanced or Metastatic Thyroid Cancer appears among the results [4]. Suberoylanilide Hydroxamic Acid in Treating Patients With Metastatic and/or Locally Advanced or Locally Recurrent Thyroid Cancer is also among the results [5].

## Related disease records

Several disease records matching "not otherwise specified" carcinoma types were also retrieved rather than trials themselves. These include Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [6]; Primary Intraosseous Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified, Derived from Odontogenic Cyst [7]; Infiltrating duct carcinoma of breast [8]; Primary Intraosseous Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified, Derived from Odontogenic Keratocyst [9]; Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [10]; Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [11]; Locally Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [12]; and Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [13].

## Supporting literature context

A MedGen concept record for Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified was retrieved alongside these disease entries [15]. A PubMed record, publication pmid 15365566, is also linked to this subject [16]. Its title is Prognostic value of morphology and hormone receptor status in breast cancer - a population-based study [14]. That paper found that among breast cancer patients, those classified with not-otherwise-specified carcinoma morphology had notably lower 5-year survival than those with special-type tumors, and that tumor morphology together with hormone receptor status remained a significant predictor of survival even after accounting for age and stage [17: "the 5-year relative survival ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma to 95% (95% CI 90-100) for special types"][17: "Morphology and hormone receptor status were confirmed as significant survival predictors in this population-based study, even after adjusting for age and stage at diagnosis"].
